description: Shared update policy. It decides by update type, never by package name: a name list is what makes a config unportable, so names stay in the repository that knows what they mean.

The line it draws: automerge whatever costs a revert when it goes wrong, and hold whatever costs data or an outage. A repository tightens this by adding automerge:false rules for its own stateful pieces, and widens it by adding minor automerge for the stateless ones.
This assumes the repository has checks worth waiting for. Renovate merges only on green, so a repo with no CI gets an automerge that proves nothing.

packageRules.description: Digest updates carry no version change - the tag already said what it wanted, and this is how a pinned SHA stays current instead of rotting.

Patches are bug fixes by definition. 14 days rather than the global 7: an automerged release is one nobody reads first, which is exactly the window a compromised package needs to be pulled from the registry.
Majors are never automerged, whatever else a repository says. A breaking change is the one case where reading the changelog IS the work.
Merging at night keeps a bad automerge from landing mid-workday, which matters most where merge means deploy.
